# @zakkster/lite-noise v1.4.0

> Zero-GC seeded Simplex 2D/3D noise, unrolled FBM, ridged/billow multifractals,
> seamless loop, tileable field, curl2, curl3, Quilez-style domain warp, and
> bakeable heightfields. Deterministic.
> Single-file ESM, ~2.24 KB min+gz, zero runtime dependencies.

## Install
npm i @zakkster/lite-noise

## Import
import {
    createNoise, Noise,
    seedNoise,
    simplex2, simplex3,
    fbm2, fbm3,
    ridged2, billow2,
    noiseLoop, tileable2,
    curl2, curl3,
    warp2,
    fillField2,
} from '@zakkster/lite-noise';

## API

- createNoise(seed = 0): Noise
    An independent noise field owning its own 512-byte permutation table. Two
    instances are two independent fields; sampling/seeding/constructing one
    never changes another. Use this to run two consumers on one page.
- new Noise(seed = 0)
    The class behind createNoise; exported for instanceof / typing.
- noise.seed(seed): this
    Re-seed an instance in place. Affects only that instance.
- noise.simplex2/simplex3/fbm2/fbm3/ridged2/billow2/noiseLoop/tileable2/curl2/curl3/warp2/fillField2
    Instance methods mirroring the module functions below. An instance at seed S
    is byte-identical to the module functions after seedNoise(S).

- seedNoise(seed = 0): void
    Rebuilds the SHARED module permutation table. Auto-seeded with 0 on module
    load. Setup cost (fills one Uint8Array in place); not on any hot path. Warns
    once in dev builds if called more than once (silent when NODE_ENV=production);
    for independent fields use createNoise instead.

- simplex2(x, y): number in ~[-1, 1]
- simplex3(x, y, z): number in ~[-1, 1]

- fbm2(x, y, octaves = 4, lacunarity = 2, gain = 0.5): number
    Unrolled 2D FBM over simplex2. Zero allocation. gain (per-octave amplitude
    decay) must be >= 0 -- the standard FBM domain, typically 0..1; a negative
    gain alternates the amplitude sign and pushes output past ~[-1, 1].
- fbm3(x, y, z, octaves = 4, lacunarity = 2, gain = 0.5): number
    Unrolled 3D FBM over simplex3. Zero allocation.

- ridged2(x, y, octaves = 4, lacunarity = 2, gain = 0.5): number    [v1.3.0]
    Ridged multifractal, (1 - |simplex|)^2 per octave over the shared FBM
    skeleton. Sharp creases at zero-crossings reaching the unit ceiling; range
    ~[0, 1], distribution skewed high. Mountains, cracked earth, veins.
    Range ~[0, 1] holds for gain >= 0 (the FBM domain); a negative gain flips the
    per-octave amplitude sign and voids the guarantee.

- billow2(x, y, octaves = 4, lacunarity = 2, gain = 0.5): number    [v1.3.0]
    Billow, |simplex| per octave over the shared skeleton. Soft absolute-value
    fold piling mass at zero, no unit spikes; range ~[0, 1]. Clouds, hills, smoke.
    Same gain >= 0 range domain as ridged2/fbm2.

- noiseLoop(t, radius = 1): number    [v1.3.0]
    Seamless periodic 1D noise -- samples a circle of radius `radius` in the 2D
    field. Drive t from 0 to 2*PI for a perfect loop: noiseLoop(0) === noiseLoop(
    2*PI) exactly (angle reduced mod 2*PI), derivative matches at the seam. Away
    from the seam, periodicity holds to a few ULPs (adding 2*PI rounds low bits).

- tileable2(x, y, periodX, periodY): number    [v1.3.0]
    Tileable 2D noise over [0, periodX) x [0, periodY). Bilinear blend of the
    sample and its three period-wrapped neighbours; opposite edges are byte-
    identical (tileable2(0, y) === tileable2(periodX, y)), so the tile is seamless
    by construction, resolution-free. Four simplex2 samples, zero allocation. The
    blend narrows the extremes, so the range sits a little inside [-1, 1].
    Precondition: periodX > 0 and periodY > 0. A period of 0 divides by 0 and
    returns a non-finite value (NaN or +/-Infinity) -- unguarded on the hot path
    (a zero tile size is a caller error, not a data-driven value); pass positive
    extents.

- curl2(x, y, out): out
    Divergence-free 2D vector. out = { x, y }, caller-owned.
    Four simplex2 samples (central-difference), precomputed 1/(2*eps).

- curl3(x, y, z, out): out    [v1.1.0]
    Divergence-free 3D vector via three offset simplex3 fields treated as
    a vector potential psi = (psi1, psi2, psi3). Curl formula:
        curl.x = d(psi3)/dy - d(psi2)/dz
        curl.y = d(psi1)/dz - d(psi3)/dx
        curl.z = d(psi2)/dx - d(psi1)/dy
    Twelve simplex3 samples per call. out = { x, y, z }, caller-owned.
    Suitable for volumetric smoke.

- warp2(x, y, strength, out): out    [v1.1.0]
    Quilez-style domain warp. Writes warped coords into out = { x, y }.
    Two fbm2 evaluations per sample using canonical offset pairs
    (5.2/1.3 and 1.7/9.2). Compose with fbm2(out.x, out.y) for the
    final warped noise value.

- fillField2(out, w, h, opts?): out    [v1.1.0]
    Bake a w * h FBM heightfield into a caller-supplied Float32Array or
    Float64Array (length >= w * h). Row-incremental coord stepping:
    `px += scale`, `py += scale` replace per-cell multiplies.
    opts (all optional, guarded so the omitted-opts path allocates
    nothing): scale = 0.01, octaves = 4, lacunarity = 2, gain = 0.5,
    ox = 0, oy = 0, normalize = false. Zero allocation.
    Range: the raw fill is amplitude-normalised but not full-range
    (~[-0.84, 0.82] at the defaults). normalize = true does a second
    in-place pass to exact [0, 1] (a colour ramp usually wants this);
    a constant field maps to all-zero. `out` is caller-owned and written
    start-to-end -- do not alias it with anything read during the call.

## Key facts

- Seeded via an inlined Mulberry32 PRNG — deterministic permutation table, zero runtime dependencies.
- No rest params, no .map, no spread anywhere on a hot path.
- Vector APIs never allocate: caller passes { x, y } or { x, y, z }.
- fillField2 accepts `opts` as either an object or omitted; the omitted-
  opts path uses `opts?.x ?? default` (zero-alloc), not `opts = {}`
  (which would allocate).
- Auto-seeded with 0 on module load; explicit seedNoise(n) is idempotent.

## Two consumers: use createNoise (important)

The module functions share ONE module-scoped permutation table. `seedNoise(n)`
mutates the SAME table every module-level consumer reads:

    // terrain
    seedNoise(42); simplex2(x, y);   // seed-42 table
    // particles (elsewhere)
    seedNoise(7);  simplex2(x, y);   // everyone now on seed-7
    // terrain
    simplex2(x, y);                  // silently changed

For a single-consumer app this is invisible. For two subsystems each wanting
their own seed stream, give each its own instance -- they cannot collide:

    const terrain   = createNoise(42);
    const particles = createNoise(7);
    terrain.simplex2(x, y);          // unaffected by anything particles does
    particles.seed(99);              // touches only particles

An instance at seed S is byte-identical to the module functions after
seedNoise(S). seedNoise warns once (dev builds) if called more than once.

## Degenerate inputs

- fbm2 / fbm3 with octaves = 0 (or negative) return 0, not NaN. This
  protects buffers baked from data-driven biome / terrain configs.
- gain must be >= 0 for fbm2 / fbm3 / ridged2 / billow2. It is the
  per-octave amplitude decay (standard FBM persistence, typically 0..1);
  a negative gain alternates the amplitude sign and pushes output past the
  documented ranges (~[-1,1] for fbm, ~[0,1] for ridged/billow). Un-guarded
  on the hot path -- gain < 0 is a caller error, not a data value.
- tileable2 requires periodX > 0 and periodY > 0; a period of 0 divides by
  zero and returns a non-finite value (NaN or +/-Infinity). Un-guarded.
- simplex2 / simplex3 with NaN or Infinity inputs return 0 (the
  truncation-to-integer path yields a plausible value rather than
  propagating NaN). Validate upstream if propagation is required.

## Output magnitudes

Measured over 100k samples at seed 42:
- simplex2 : max |v| ~= 0.998        (docs "approx. [-1, 1]")
- simplex3 : max |v| ~= 0.976
- curl2    : mean |v| ~= 3.4         (scale ~0.005 inputs)
- curl3    : mean |v| ~= 3.8, max ~= 10.6
- curl3 divergence residual: ~0.6% of |v| — finite-difference floor

Scale curl outputs before writing to particle velocities.

## Determinism goldens (seed = 42)

FNV-1a 32-bit over Float32 bytes:
- 256x256 default fillField2  -> ddef5970
- 128x128 warp2 + fbm2        -> ca4f9f1e
- 32x32x8 curl3 slab (packed) -> 1ac7a518
- 128x128 ridged2             -> 2342c230    [v1.3.0]
- 128x128 billow2             -> acf96355    [v1.3.0]
- 64x64 period-4 tileable2    -> b6d00662    [v1.3.0]
- 720-sample noiseLoop        -> 2cfa58f8    [v1.3.0]

Any change to a golden is a breaking change and must be called out in
CHANGELOG.md. Regenerate: `npm run goldens`.

## Zero-GC gate (falsifiable, not asserted)

`npm run torture` (node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs) gates every hot path
with lite-gc-profiler's measureOps/checkOps under `stabilize: true` and rules
`{ maxBytesPerOp: 2, maxMajorsPerKOp: 0 }`, over both the module functions and
the instance methods. The 2 B/op ceiling matches lite-gc-profiler's docs-
recommended tier for 1K+ ops (V8 IC / feedback-vector floor); the strict zero-
majors rule catches any real allocation that hides under the byte-budget noise.
Heavy bakes (fillField2, incl. the normalize pass) are gated on major-GC count
and ArrayBuffer retention instead of per-op bytes. `NOISE_TORTURE_BREAK=1` must
make the gate exit non-zero -- proof it can bite. A real leak crosses both bars.

## Bundle budget

~2.24 KB minified + gzipped (2,291 B), self-contained with zero runtime
dependencies, enforced via `npm run bundle-check` (esbuild --minify,
nothing externalised; ceiling 2,560 B). ridged2/billow2 share the octave
skeleton with fbm2 (via `_octaves2`); noiseLoop and tileable2 are new code.
New variants must share the skeleton or they don't ship.

## Usage sketches

// Terrain heightmap, zero alloc per frame
seedNoise(42);
const field = new Float32Array(256 * 256);
fillField2(field, 256, 256, { scale: 0.01, octaves: 6 });

// Curl flow field for particles (2D)
const v = { x: 0, y: 0 };
for (let i = 0; i < particles.length; i++) {
    curl2(particles[i].x * 0.005, particles[i].y * 0.005, v);
    particles[i].vx = v.x;
    particles[i].vy = v.y;
}

// Volumetric smoke velocity (3D)
const v3 = { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 };
curl3(px * 0.02, py * 0.02, pz * 0.02, v3);

// Warped FBM ("cloudy terrain") in two calls
const warped = { x: 0, y: 0 };
warp2(x * 0.01, y * 0.01, 1.5, warped);
const value = fbm2(warped.x, warped.y);

// Ridged mountains, normalized to [0,1] for a colour ramp
const height = new Float32Array(256 * 256);
const terrain = createNoise(42);
let i = 0;
for (let y = 0; y < 256; y++)
    for (let x = 0; x < 256; x++)
        height[i++] = terrain.ridged2(x * 0.01, y * 0.01, 6);

// Perfect animation loop -- t sweeps 0..2*PI, closes seamlessly
const angle = (frame / TOTAL_FRAMES) * Math.PI * 2;
const wobble = noiseLoop(angle, 1.5);

// Seamless tiling texture, period 4 in noise space
const W = 256;
const tex = new Float32Array(W * W);
let t = 0;
for (let y = 0; y < W; y++)
    for (let x = 0; x < W; x++)
        tex[t++] = tileable2(x / W * 4, y / W * 4, 4, 4);  // wraps edge-to-edge

## Ecosystem recipes (v1.4.0)

Runnable, CI-tested integration recipes in examples/ (NOT shipped in the
tarball). Each adds ZERO runtime dependency -- the peers are devDependencies and
each recipe holds its own createNoise instance, so two on one page never collide.

- curl2 -> lite-particles advection (examples/curl-advection.mjs). The seam needs
  no API from either side: an Emitter onUpdate(p, dt) hook samples curl2 into a
  pre-allocated {x,y} and writes p.vx/p.vy. Both curl2 and Emitter.update are
  0 B/call, so the combined loop is zero-alloc.
- fillField2 -> lite-gl field (examples/field-to-gl.mjs). A baked Float32Array is
  exactly a GL instance buffer. Packs one LAYOUT.POINT instance per cell (stride
  8: x,y,size,r,g,b,a,_pad -- lite-gl LAYOUT.POINT === lite-particles POINT_STRIDE)
  and proves the handoff by a BIT-EXACT round-trip (bake -> field.push -> read
  field.data back -> byte-identical). The live GPU upload/readback is lite-gl's
  own tested territory: sink.upload(field.data, 0, count*8, 0, 8).
- curl ambient behavior (examples/ambient-curl.mjs). registerBehavior('CURL', ...)
  whose tick advances particles through a curl field. Registration + the pure
  advance() physics are CI-tested headless; createAmbientFX(canvas, ...) and the
  draw calls are browser-only. ambient-fx keeps its zero-dep pledge -- recipe,
  not dependency.
- N1 composability, asserted at the integration level: two instance-backed flows
  interleaved in one process produce byte-identical trajectories to each run
  alone.

## Dependencies

- None (production). Seed provenance is an inlined Mulberry32 PRNG.
- @zakkster/lite-gc-profiler  (dev only, gate on zero-alloc)
- @zakkster/lite-patternforge (dev only, seamlessScore cross-check for tileable2)
- @zakkster/lite-particles, @zakkster/lite-gl, @zakkster/lite-ambient-fx
  (dev only, the v1.4.0 ecosystem-seam recipes; no runtime dep added)
